<val> exceed with <un>, the suffix <in> for more than one person; {zah valun} is beyond the measure
village in Falam township of Chin State, named as the far end of the area where the Zo dialect is spoken

placed after a verb: with a repeated or swinging movement or sound, or with strong feeling; {ging valval} is keep ringing and {duh valval} is crave strongly; after a number it is doubled <val>, well over
<val>, more than, and <vei>, times, written as one word after a number: over that many times

terms: be more than enough/be in excess
definition: <val> exceed with <zaw>, more
<va>, go and, and <man>, seize, written as one word
a small plump ground bird, also called {mimva}; set against the eagle as the weak one
plural form: quails, the birds God sent as food for Israel in the wilderness
<va>, go and, and <mu>, see, written as one word: go and see
<va>, bird, with <mul>, feather: a feather of a bird, here as an ornament stuck into the hair, worn with the verb <tot>
the sky and heaven above the earth; {van leh lei} is heaven and earth
things that are bought, sold, carried or used, as in {van man}, the price of goods, and {van tuamtuam}, various things; not the sky
<van>, heaven, at the start of a clause; {van nuai} is under heaven
the English word van with <mawtaw>, motor vehicle: a van, a closed vehicle for goods or passengers; <van> is here not the Zolai word for sky
<van>, heaven or sky, with the ending <a>, of or in: of the sky, as in {vana vasate}, the birds of the air, and {vana aksi}, the stars of the sky
<van>, heaven or sky, with the place marker <ah>; {vanah vasate} are the birds of the air
<van>, goods, and <bawl>, make, written as one word: make goods or things; also said of those who make them, as in {vanbawl mipil te}
the making of goods, or a place where goods are made
a city on the west coast of Canada
<van> heaven with <daitui> dew and the plural <te>

terms: look upward/look up to the sky
definition: <van> sky with <dak>, look up
<van>, sky, with <dawn>, top: high up in the sky; {vandawn ah} is in the air, said of aircraft in flight and of smoke that rises
taken as <vaan.2> and <ding> written as one word: to attend to or take charge of affairs; {vai vanding in} is in order to attend to the affairs
village named among the villages of the Tedim area

<van>, sky, and <dum>, blue, written as one word: the blue sky, and the colour sky blue
<va> and <nei> written as one word: go to a place and hold or carry out something there, as a speech or an inspection
an opening, hole or gap; {kong vang} is a gate or doorway, {han vang} the mouth of a tomb, and {kulh vang} a gap in a wall
power or might, and the shining glory of God; {minthanna vang} is glorious splendour, and {a vang lian} means he is powerful
used after <ma> or <maa>, the way ahead: {ma vang} is to go forward well, to succeed in what one does

<vang> opening with <ah>, at or into the opening; {phim vangah} is through the eye of a needle and {han kong vangah} at the mouth of the tomb
<van>, heaven, with <gam>, country: heaven as the land where God is

plural of <vangik>, burden
the things a person owns, goods and valuables
<van> sky with <gin> sound; written {vangin’na}, with the noun suffix <na>, for thunder
<vang> power with the marker <in>: {vaihawmna le vangin ngaihsun} is to count something as counsel and might

thunder, the loud sound from the sky in a storm; from <van>, sky, and <ging>, sound
plural of <vanging>, thunder: peals of thunder, often named together with <khuaphialepte>, flashes of lightning
word of songs and poetic speech for the village or town where one was born and belongs; {Dimtui vangkhua} is a poetic name of Tedim
placed after a verb: the thing really does happen or is so, often against what might be expected
<vanglian>, be mighty, in the form used before a suffix, with <huai>, worthy of: awe-inspiring

<vanglian>, be mighty, in the form used before a suffix, with <tuak>, be fitting: fit to be mighty
<vang>, power, with <lian>, great: having great power; {a vanglian Topa} is the Lord Almighty
capitalised as a title of God: <Vanglian Pasian>, God Almighty

<vanglian>, mighty, with the ending <in>: being mighty, in a mighty way
<vanglian>, mighty, with <pa>, male person: a mighty man, a warrior or hero
a title of God in present-day religious writing, often as {Tawntung Vanglianpa}, the Eternal Mighty One; not a human warrior or hero
<vanglianpa> written with a capital, title of God
title of God, literally the most powerful; {Vanglianpen Topa} renders the Lord Almighty or the Lord of hosts

plural form of <vanglian>, the mighty ones, or after a plural noun as in {kumpi vangliante}, mighty kings
<vanglian> mighty with <zaw> more
form of <vanglian> used before <zawk>, <nading>, <mahmahna> and the like

the greatness and splendour of God that is shown to people
plural of <vangliatna>, power; beings or forces that hold power, in heaven or on earth
plural of <vangliatna>, power: deeds that show the power of God, miracles
<vang>, power or glory, with <nei>, have, written as one word: having power, effect or honour
the having of power and standing among people, named together with fame and with skill in leading; {thatang' vangneihna} is power by force, hard power
<vang> power with <nei> have and the plural <te>: those who have power; in Galatians 4:3 of the spiritual powers ruling the air

<vangneu> small opening with the plural <te>
<vang> power with <pi> great
used with <ma> or <lampi>, the way ahead: make a journey or undertaking succeed

terms: make an opening/make a hole/open up
definition: <vang>, hole or opening, with the causative <sak>: make a hole or opening in something, as for smoke to go out or for people to get through; not make a journey succeed

shining glory, usually after <minthanna>; {a vangtaang} is glorious
plural of <vang>, opening; {kong vangte} is gates, {tawlet vangte} is windows
a Zomi village in the Tedim area of Chin State; in lists it follows the name of a person to show the home village
another spelling of <vantung>, heaven, the dwelling place of God
<vangtung>, heaven, with the place marker <ah>: in the sky, in heaven
<vangtung>, heaven, with <mi>, person: an angel, a messenger from heaven; another spelling of <vantungmi>
placed after a verb to show that the action is done strongly or without letting go; {kap vangvang} is wail bitterly
<van>, goods, with <hoih>, good: goods of good quality, fine belongings
<van>, goods, with <hoihlo>, not good, written as one word: goods of poor quality
<van>, goods or things, and <honkhat>, some, written as one word: a number of things or objects
one of the descendants of Bani who had married a foreign wife in the time of Ezra
move the hand through the air as a sign, with the linking ending <in>; {a khut vanin} is waving or motioning with the hand; also written <vaanin>
a person who calls up the spirits of the dead; often as {vankah thei}, one who is able to do this

<vankah>, medium, with the plural <te>

<vankahthei>, medium, with the plural <te>

<van>, thing, with <khai>, hang: a peg or hook on which things are hung
<van>, things, with <khai>, hang, and the noun suffix <na>: a peg or hook to hang things on
plural of <vankhaina>, a thing on which something is hung or fastened, as the hooks and clasps of the tabernacle
<van>, goods, with <khak>, send: goods sent to someone, a parcel
goods that the law forbids; in the news mostly narcotic drugs, also <vankham zatui>

<vankham> with the plural <te>
<vankham>, illegal drugs, and <zuak>, sell, written as one word: sell drugs, and before a noun the one who sells them, as in {vankhamzuak mi}, drug dealer
<van>, here a thing or article, and <khat> written as one word: a thing, one object
<van>, here goods, things, and <khatpeuh>, any one, written as one word: any article or object whatever
<van>, here goods or things, and <khempeuh> written as one word: all the things, every article
<van>, goods, and <kholna>, place of storing, written as one word: a place where goods are stored; also said of a place where data is kept
goods taken in war; the other text has <vankila> in the same verse, so this may be a misprint of it
goods taken by enemies, set beside {mat ding mi}, people to be captured
<van>, goods, with <kila>, taken: goods taken in war
the middle of the sky, the open air above the earth; used with <lai-ah>: {vankim lai-ah} is in midair
<vankim>, the middle of the sky, written with a capital at the start of a sentence
<van>, goods, with <kinusia>, left behind: goods left by a defeated enemy
goods left behind by a defeated enemy and taken by the victors
<van>, goods, and <kisam>, be needed, written as one word: the things that are needed, supplies
<van>, goods, with <kisut>, be plundered, and the plural <te>: goods taken by force
<van>, goods, and <kizuakna>, place of sale, written as one word: a place where goods are sold
<van>, goods, with <koihna>, place of keeping: a storehouse or storeroom, often as {vankoihna inn}
not a building or room but a thing or part in which goods are kept, such as a bag, a cupboard, the boot of a car or the lockers over the seats of a plane
<vankoihna>, storehouse, with the plural <te>

terms: vault of the sky/dome of heaven
definition: <van> sky with <kuum>, arch or vault, and <pi>, great: the sky seen as a great cover over the earth
<van>, sky, with <lai>, middle: the height of the sky where the eagle flies, {mu vanlai}; in present-day writing also outer space
<van>, here goods, and <lak>, midst, written as one word: among the things someone carries, the luggage of a traveller; {vanlak panin} is from the luggage
<van>, goods, with <lak>, taken, and the plural <te>: the things taken in war
<van>, sky, with <lam>, direction: the direction of the sky, upward; in war news the air as against <leilam>, the ground, so that {vanlam pan kap} is to attack from the air
<vanlam>, the sky side, and <pan>, from: from the air, said of attacks, bombing and reinforcement by aircraft; it stands before the verb and contrasts with {leilam pan}, on the ground
<van>, goods, with <lei>, buy; <vanlei vanzuak> is buying and selling, trade

<vanlei>, buy goods, with the noun suffix {-na}: the buying of goods, or the place where goods are bought, a shop; {vanzuak vanleina} is buying and selling, trade
<van>, goods, with <lei>, buy, and <pa> marking a male person; set against <vanzuakpa>, the seller
<vanlei>, buy goods, with the plural <te>: those who buy
<van>, sky, <le>, and, <lei>, earth, written as one word; {vanlelei kikalah} is between sky and earth, in midair
{van le nate}, goods and things, written as one word: the goods and things that a person or a household has or needs
<van>, sky, with the verb fly, <leeng>: a machine that flies
<vanleng>, aeroplane, and <khawlna>, stopping place: an airport or airfield

<vanleng>, aeroplane, and <tuahsiatna>, misfortune or accident: the crash of an aircraft, the usual term of news reports

<vanleng>, aeroplane, and <hawlpa>, driver, written as one word: the man who flies an aeroplane
<vanlenghawl>, flying an aeroplane, with <zah>, amount, written as one word: how much a pilot has flown, counted in hours
<vanleng>, aeroplane, and <khat>, one or a, written as one word

<vanleng>, aircraft, with <neu>, small: a light plane, and in one report an unmanned drone

<vanleng>, aeroplane, with <tual>, open ground: the place where aeroplanes land and take off

definition: <vanleng>, aeroplane, and <tung>, on, written as one word: on or aboard an aircraft
<vanleng> and <zong> written as one word: the aeroplane also, even the plane

<vanpi>, the heavens, with the plural <te>

<van>, goods, with <sia>, bad, written as one word: things that are broken, spoiled or destroyed

<van>, heaven, with the plural <te>

apparently a misprint of <vantungmi>, angel
the dwelling place of God and the angels
the sky above the earth, where the birds fly and from which the rain falls
<vantung> written with a capital, mostly in {Vantung Gam}, the kingdom of heaven
<vantung>, heaven, with the place ending <a>: in heaven, in the sky; {vantunga om} is that is in heaven
<vantung>, heaven, with the place marker <ah>

<vantung>, heaven, with <mi>, person: a messenger from heaven, an angel

placed after a verb for hurried, restless or rushing movement: rushing, pounding
doubled form of <van>, stretch out the hands, again and again

<vanzuak>, sell goods, with the noun suffix <na>; {vanzuakna phual} is a marketplace

<vanzuak>, sell goods, with <pa>, marking a man: the seller, set against <Vanleipa>, the buyer

definition: <va> and <paithei> written as one word: be able to go to another place

terms: go and reach/visit in person/go to
definition: <va> with a verb that means reach, written as one word: go to a place and arrive there, mostly of leaders who visit the place itself
the great hornbill, a large forest bird; the Zomi take it as their emblem and as a picture of faithfulness

<va> bird with <pi> big: large bird; in the verses always {gun vapi}, river big bird, for the stork
<va> and <pia> written as one word: go to someone and give; {tha vapia} is go and encourage
plural of <vapi>, large bird; {gun vapite} and {tui vapite}, large water birds, are used for the stork and the ibis

terms: go and deliver/take to/go and send

a place on the Kalay to Falam and Hakha road in Chin State, Myanmar, with a bridge over the Manipur River and an army camp
a bird of any kind
<vasa>, bird, with <bu>, nest
<vasabu>, nest, at the start of a sentence
<sam> call with <va> before it, marking going over to do it
<vasa>, bird, with the ending {-no} for the young of an animal: a young or small bird
<vasa>, bird, with the plural <te>

queen of Persia, wife of King Xerxes, who lost her place as queen when she refused to come before the king
a kind of small bird, <va>; the exact kind is not settled
<va>, go and, with <sim.3>, attack, written as one word: go to a place and attack it, of armed groups and armies
<va>, go and, with <sim>, here visit or take part in, written as one word: go to a festival or gathering and join in it
strike a person or attack a place, of God, a fighter or an army; {namsau tawh vat} is strike with the sword
after a verb, not the verb strike: the action comes suddenly or unexpectedly, as {phawk vat} suddenly remember and {si vat} die suddenly; often with {thakhat thu in} or <mawk>
cut down the trees and bush of a field before burning it, as {lo vat} clear a field; not a striking of a person or place
a wild plant with a vine, <gui>, and gourds, <umgah>, not fit to eat
kind of bird; in the lists of unclean birds {gam vatawt} and {tui vatawt} stand where English has owl, swan, pelican or gull
<vatawt>, duck, with <tui> as in <aktui>, egg: the egg of a duck
<vat>, strike, with <gawp>, thoroughly: strike down or defeat completely
<vatgawp>, strike down, with the linking ending {-in}
the city state in Rome that is the seat of the Pope and of the Roman Catholic Church
<vat>, strike, with the linking ending <in>: striking or having struck; often {namsau tawh vatin}, with the sword
after a verb, of something that comes on abruptly; {khuamial hong suak vatin}, darkness came suddenly
<vat> strike with <khia>, out, away, and the suffix <in>
strike so that the person dies, often with the sword
kill or defeat in great numbers, as with a sword
of trees and grass, after <singkung> or <lopa>: cut all the growth of a piece of land down to the ground, named together with <haltumna>, burning; not a killing of people
<vatmai>, strike down, with <pa>, the male one who does it: a {vatmaipa} is he who struck down

<vat> strike with <mang>, away, gone: strike so that the person is no more; of death taking the children from the streets

<vat>, strike, with <tuk>, fall: strike so that the person falls
<vat> strike with <tum>, completely; said of the sword
<va>, bird, with <tuang>, ride: of a bird, sit on the top of a tree
<va> and <tung> written as one word: go and arrive at another place
placed after a verb: the action is done in a sudden, hasty or jerky way, without holding back, often again and again; {lungtom vatvat} is quick to flare up
frighten someone with words of what will be done to him, so that he does or gives something
words or acts that threaten harm to make someone obey or stop, or a stern warning; {vauna ngah} is receive threats
placed after a verb or describing word to say that a smell, a sound or a desire is strong and keeps on: {namtui vauvau} is strongly fragrant, {ham vauvau} is buzz on and on, {duh vauvau} is crave
a district of London in England
placed after a verb: doing it with force, strongly or noisily, much like <baba>

terms: go visiting/go about/go for a walk
definition: <va>, go and, with <vak>, go about, written as one word: go out to another place and walk about or visit there

form of <vua>, beat, with {-ua} changed to {-aw}, used before a negative: {hong vaw kei e} is did not beat me
give a name, with <min>, name: {min vawh} is to name a person, an animal or a place

form of <vawh> with the linking suffix <in>, putting a saddle or load on a pack animal
form of <vawh> with the linking suffix <in>, sowing seed
<vawh>, sow, with <pa>, marking a man: the man who sows, in {khaici vawhpa}
<vawh> sow with <sa>, already done; {na vawhsa an} is the crop you have sown
in {laa van vawhsak}, put the gear on a donkey for someone, saddle it
<vawhsak> saddle for someone with the linking ending <in>
<vawh>, sow, with the plural <te>: the people who sow seed

terms: be able to put through/be able to thread
definition: <vawh>, thread or put a cord through, with <zo>, be able: be able to pass a cord through, as through the nose of an animal; not from <vawh> call or sow
<va>, go and, with <zin>, travel, written as one word: go to another place on a journey or a visit
in {gun vazonei}, a river bird in the list of unclean birds
<va> and <zuak> written as one word: go to another place and sell something there
<va> and <zuan> written as one word: go off toward a place
<va>, go and, and <zui>, follow, written as one word: go to where others are going and follow them, go along
sentence-final particle of emphasis or urging; after a command, often as {dih ve}, it presses the hearer to go ahead, and after <hi>, as {hi ve’n}, it stresses a statement
the particles <ve>, emphasis, and <maw>, question, together at the end of a sentence in place of <hi>: the speaker states something with feeling and looks for agreement, or wonders at it
sentence-final words after <hi> in the speech of one person about himself, here I would surely have given; apparently an emphatic <ve> with a shortened first person ending
<ve> and <cin> written as one word at the end of a sentence addressed to you, after <hi>: an emphatic you are, you know
a part of a town or village; {Naioth veeng} is the Naioth quarter of Ramah
a person or household living near one's own, as in {ka veeng khat}, one of my neighbours; the pair {veeng leh paam} is the neighbours all around

the tenth of the appointed positions of a Zomi household: one of the neighbours with whom the house gets on best; two neighbours may hold the position for each other, and he shares the duties of the <beh thusa>
<veeng>, a quarter or neighbourhood of a town, with the place marker <ah>, in or to: {Naioth veengah} is in Naioth, a quarter of Ramah; <veeng> is the long-vowel spelling of <veng>
<veeng>, neighbour, and <pa>, which marks a man, written as one word: the man who lives next door
plural of <veeng>; {inn veengte} is those who live in the houses nearby
listed by the book as one entry with <khawval>, so taken as a word of the same meaning: not serious or self-controlled in behaviour; the page gives no sentence
second word of Las Vegas, a city in the state of Nevada in the United States
go to see someone who is sick or in need and care for them; said also of God coming to help his people
sentence-final word of exclamation that calls attention to something happening now, as in listen, people are crying out

a sentence-final word written like <veh>, visit, but not that verb, with the exclamation <aw>: closes a spoken sentence with feeling or emphasis; after <kei>, not, as in {hi kei veh aw}, it protests or insists

the sentence-final words <veh.2> and <ee.2> together: closes a spoken remark with surprise, sudden notice or admiration, as English why or how at its start; it follows the verb or <kei>, not, and takes the place of <hi>
noun from <veh>, visit: a visit to the sick, to prisoners or to those in need; also the money or gift brought on such a visit
an occasion or instance, counted with a number word before it: {khat vei} is once, {thum vei} is three times
have an illness, with the name of the illness or <natna> before it
the left as opposed to <ziat> and <tak>, the right; {vei lam} is the left-hand side

terms: no fewer than/as many as/all of
definition: <vei>, time or occasion, with <vilvel>, a word of emphasis: placed after a number, it stresses that the thing happened that many times, fully and distinctly; {thum vei vilvel} is three whole times, no fewer than three times
<vei>, time, and <bang>, about, written as one word after a number: about that many times, as in {3 veibang}, some three times
gas passed from the bowels; {veih pek} is break wind
move an offering to and fro before the Lord; {veii-a biakna} is a wave offering
a heart that is burdened for something and cares deeply about it; {minam veiina} is concern for one's people
using the left hand rather than the right; said of Ehud and of the slingers of Benjamin
the left-hand side; before a noun it means left, as in {veilam khut}, left hand

terms: on the left/at the left side
definition: <veilam>, left side, with the place ending <a>, at or on: {ka veilama} is on my left
<veilam>, the left side, with the place ending {-ah}; often paired with <taklam>, the right
<veilam> left side with the suffix <in>; {a khut veilamin} is with his left hand

terms: not suffer from/not be concerned about
definition: <vei>, here a verb, be sick with or be burdened in heart for, with <lo>, not, written as one word: not fall ill, or not care about a matter; another word than {sau veilo}, before long
<vei>, time, with <na>: after a number word it gives the order of an occasion, {a nih veina} is the second time
particle showing number of times
<vei>, feel concern for, with <na>: heartfelt concern or burden for people, a nation or a cause, not a count of times; it stands beside <itna>, love, and in {minam veina}, concern for the nation
<veina> and <takpi> written as one word: real heartfelt concern
plural of <veina> in the sense of a thing one suffers from or is burdened about, from <vei>, suffer or feel concern
<vei>, suffer from a disease, with <pa>, the man who does so: the person who has the disease
<vei>, time or occasion, and the topic marker <pen> written as one word: this time, or after a number the occasions counted, as the thing spoken about

terms: care about most/be most concerned for
definition: <vei>, here feel concern or a burden for, with <pen> as the superlative ending: what one cares about most
<vei>, time, with the intensive <pi>: after <sau> or <sawt>, long, it means for a very long time
<vei>, time, with the intensive <pi>: after <tam>, many, it means many times, again and again
<vei>, time, and <piang>, happen, written as one word after a number: happened that many times
<vei>, suffer from a sickness, with the causative <sak>: make someone suffer from a disease, as Satan afflicted Job with sores; not from <vei> time
<vei>, time, with the distributive ending {-ta}, each: after a number, that many times in every period named; {kum khat in khat veita} is once a year
<vei> and <tak> written as one word after a number: that many times, stressing that the number is large; {7 veitak} is as many as seven times
<vei>, suffer from a sickness, with the plural <te>: those who have a disease
<vei>, time, and <tuak.2>, each, written as one word after a number: so many times each, as of strokes of the cane given to each person
<vei>, times, and <val>, more than, written as one word after a number: more than that many times
used after <khat>: {khat veivei}, sometimes, now and then; said twice for sometimes this, sometimes that
without <khat> before it, move something to and fro again and again, as hands waved in the air or a cradle rocked
<veivei>, at times, and <ciangin>, when: always after <khat> as {khat veivei ciangin}, sometimes, at the head of a sentence or clause
<vei> time with <zaw>, more; {nihvei sangin a tam veizaw} is more than twice
{a vek-a} is all of it, the whole together
{a vek-in} follows a list and sums it up: all of them, the whole
the whole of it, used after <a> or <i>, as in {a vekin} all of it, all of them, {i vekin} all of us
the whole, everyone or everything together, used as {a vekpi-in} or {a vekpi-un}
<vekpi>, all, and <gawm>, add together: all added together; stands after the thing counted and before the number, and heads the last line of a list of sums
<vekpi>, all, with the linking <a> written with a hyphen; {a vekpi-a} is all of them together
<vekpi>, the whole, with the ending <in>; {a vekpi-in} is altogether, in all, before a total
<vekpi> and <gawm> written as one word: all added together, used before a total number
<vekpi> all with plural <te>: {ko mi vekpite} is all of us the people
<vekpi> all with <un>, usually written {vekpi-un}
used as {a vekun}, all of them together, with a plural subject
look at something closely to find out its condition, as a priest examines a disease or scouts look over a land
<vel>, examine, with <cian>, carefully, written as one word: look a thing over thoroughly
<vel>, examine, with <cian>, carefully, and the noun suffix {-na}: a close examination; {velcianna nei} is carry out an inspection
particle at the end of a spoken sentence that adds emphasis or feeling, as in {a hoih pah ei vele}; probably <ve> with a further ending
<vel> in the sense strike, not examine, with <gawp>, severely, written as one word: beat a person badly
<vel>, examine, with the linking ending <in>, joining it to the next verb
<vel> examine with <kik>, again
<vel>, examine, with the noun suffix {-na}: the examining of a patient; {ha velna} is a dental check
<vel> with <sak>: look a thing or a person over for someone, as a doctor examines a patient; {ki velsak} is have oneself examined
follows <na> pain, {na sa} feel pain, {na sak} cause pain or <kha> bitter: with intense, sharp suffering
general intensifier after a verb or descriptive word of any kind, not only after words of pain: {cidam velval} is quite healthy and {lumlet velval} is overturn completely
<velval>, bitterly, with the noun suffix <na>; {nat velvalna} is sharp, severe pain
<velval>, bitterly, severely, with the causative <sak>; {thuk velvalsak} is turn sharply sour, of the stomach
reduplicated adverb placed after a verb; with <phe> it describes hair waving or flowing loosely
<vel>, look over, doubled for continued action: look at a thing again and again, or go through things one after another, as against the adverb {velvel} that follows another verb
<ve> and <maw> written as one word at the end of a request: a friendly urging, do so, won't you
written {ven’} before <ciangin> or <theih>, of a plague or a time of mourning coming to an end
sentence-final word after a command with <dih>, urging the hearer to do it
sentence-final word after <hi> in a statement, not after a command: it stresses that the thing is plainly so, and may be followed by <maw> or <cin>
<ven>, surely, and <maw>, the questioning or exclaiming word: sentence-final after <hi> or a verb, it states something as plain and asks the hearer to agree, like English isn't it so or don't you see
keeping people safe by watching over them, as soldiers or the law protect civilians

terms: when it ceased/when it was over
definition: <ven>, cease or subside, and <ciang>, when, written as one word: when a war or trouble had come to an end
words that close a clause and state it as plain to see or only to be expected: after all, as one can see, of course; the clause often gives the ground for what is said next
a country in South America
of a plague, trouble or season, to come to an end and be gone
the part of a village or town where one lives, and the people who live near
ending of a sentence in which the speaker talks of himself with feeling, after <kei> or <hi> as in {kei veng} and {hi veng}; not the noun for a neighbourhood and not the verb cease
capitalised form of <veng>, a quarter or section of a town, in {Veng Nihna}, the Second or New Quarter of Jerusalem
<veng>, neighbourhood, and <kim>, the area around: the neighbourhood and what lies round it; mostly in the doubled expression {veng kim veng pam}, all around where one lives, with <pam>, vicinity
<veng>, neighbourhood, and <pam>, edge: used in the paired expression {veng kim veng pam}, the whole neighbourhood round about where one lives
<veng>, neighbourhood, with <thusa>: the tenth of the appointed household positions of Zo custom, a neighbour with whom the house is on good terms, who works beside the <beh thusa>
<veng>, quarter or neighbourhood, with the place ending {-a}: in the quarter, of the quarter
<veng>, a quarter or neighbourhood of a town, with the place marker <ah>, in or to: {Naioth vengah} is in Naioth, a quarter of Ramah
guard a person or a life so that it is safe; <veng>, here guard, with <bit>, safe
<vengbit>, protect, with the noun suffix <na>: the protecting of a person or a right, mostly as {vengbitna ding}, in order to protect
<veng>, neighbourhood, and <bup>, whole, written as one word
<veng> cease, come to an end, with the suffix <in>; {pawi vengin} is when the feast was over
<veng> and <khat> written as one word: a neighbourhood, one quarter of a town
<veng> and <kuam> written as one word: a neighbourhood or residential area of a town, the district where people live
<veng>, <le> and <paam> written as one word: the neighbourhood and its surroundings, and the people who live there
<veng>, cease, with <nailo>, not yet, written as one word: of trouble or fighting, not yet at an end
a male neighbour, or a fellow man
<veng>, cease, and <pak>, soon, written as one word: of trouble, come to an end soon; mostly with a negative
<veng>, neighbourhood, and <pan>, from, written as one word after the name of a quarter
<veng>, cease, with <pan>, here only then, written as one word: of a war or of fighting, stop at last
<veng>, cease, with the causative <sak>: bring a trouble, hardship or disease to an end
<veng> and <sung> written as one word: the inside of a neighbourhood; after a place name, the area of that name

terms: in the neighbourhood/in the area of
definition: <veng> and <sungah> written as one word, after a place name: in that quarter, district or neighbourhood
<vengsung>, neighbourhood, and <teng>, all, written as one word: the whole of a neighbourhood; after a place name, all around that area
<veng>, neighbourhood, with {-ta}, as in <lawmta>: people who live next to each other, neighbours in their relation to one another
<veng>, cease, and <ta>, now or already, written as one word: a matter or case is finished, is cleared
the people living near someone; also used of a single neighbor
<veng> and <tuamtuam> written as one word: the several quarters or districts of a town
placed after a verb or describing word: standing out high above the ordinary; {sang vengvang} is towering, {pil vengvang} outstandingly clever and {sin so vengvang} be boiling with anger
in {kut vengvangna}, the loud groaning of the wounded; the other text has <vengvengna> in the same verse
<veng> doubled, after <a>: each neighbourhood or quarter for itself, quarter by quarter
in {kut vengvengna}, the loud groaning of the wounded; the other text has <vengvangna> in the same verse
placed after a verb for a noisy and widespread stir: {so vengvung} is seethe in uproar, {buai vengvung} is be in a commotion
<ve> and <ni> written as one word at the end of a sentence: let us, an invitation or urging that includes the speaker; often as {dih veni}
<ven>, cease, with the causative <sak>: make a trouble, dispute or hardship come to an end
a hospital machine that breathes for a patient who cannot breathe alone
the planet Venus; as the morning star it is called <zingsol>
after a verb, shows a great amount or degree: piled up, laden, intensely
a state in the north-east of the United States of America
a numbered verse of a holy book, written before or after its number
one form of a text, a translation or a program among several, as an English version of a statement or a version of the Bible
emphatic word after a verb: at all, even, just; with <lo> or <kei>, not at all; with <leh>, expresses a wish, if only

closes an exclamation addressed to the hearer, often followed by <aw>: <ve> with <teh>, here not when; the speaker remarks on what the hearer is or does, as in {manglua veteh-aw}, you really obey too much
<vet> and <kei> written as one word after a verb: not at all; before <in> it forbids, do not at all
<vet>, at all, with the first person negative ending that is short for {kei ing}, written as one word after a verb: I do not at all, I never
the emphatic <vet> and <lo>, not, written as one word: placed after a verb, not at all, not in the least
<vet> and <loh> written as one word after a verb: not at all; the form taken before <ding>, <hi> and <na>, and {gen vetloh} is not even to be spoken of
the right of one member or office to stop a decision, mostly as {veto power}
<vet> and <se> written as one word: emphatic particle after a verb or describing word, really, indeed; after <lo>, not at all

expressive word placed after a verb such as <tuang>, ride, <tuto>, sit up on, or <dakkhia>, look out: it seems to picture something perched up on top or sticking out above in plain view; the exact sense is to be confirmed
placed after a verb for something that keeps coming steadily, as steam or a good smell rising from food; also of an action done again and again
placed after a verb to show that the action goes on with great force or intensity, as of running fast, glowing hot or the sun beating down
all the same, in spite of that; placed after a verb, often following a clause with <hangin>, although

terms: all the same/still anyway/just the same
definition: <veve>, still, nevertheless, and <lel>, just, merely, not the verb lose: placed after a verb and before the sentence-final word, the thing holds all the same in spite of what was said before, often after a clause with <hangin> or <zong>
<veve> and <ding> written as one word, after a verb: will do or be so all the same
<veve>, nevertheless, and <lai>, still, written as one word after a verb: the action still goes on in spite of what was said before
<veve> and <mawk> written as one word after a verb: all the same, even so, often of something unwelcome or unexpected
<veve> still, all the same, with the noun suffix <na>: the fact of doing something nevertheless; {amah a phat vevena uh} is that they went on praising him all the same
<veve>, all the same, with the ending {-sam} written as one word, after a verb: it was done or is so all the same
<veve> still, all the same, with plural <te>: those who do so all the same, in {a zuau vevete}, those who lie even after swearing an oath
words of urging at the end of a sentence addressed to several people, <ve> with the plural command ending: do go ahead, please do; often followed by <leh>
put a band or ring around something; of a snake, coil around
after a verb of speaking or acting against someone, as <ci> say, <phih> spit or <peek> kick: do it with scorn or insolence; exact force not confirmed
going round in a circle, said of a band or rim
one going round or one trip there and back, counted with a number as {vial khat}, one round, and {vial nih}, two rounds
village in the Tonzang area of northern Chin State in Myanmar
<vial>, bind around, with <cip>, tightly: wrap closely all round

terms: the one who wrapped it round
definition: <vialcip> wrap around with <pa>, male person
of ropes, be wound around someone
<vial>, wind or twist something round, with the linking marker <in>; said of ropes round the head and of thorns twisted into a crown
<vial>, a turn around, with <khat>, one: one full round, as of the moon around the earth or a train around its loop
<vial>, coil around, with <lum>, to death: of a snake, kill by coiling around the victim
<vial>, used after <ci> say of mocking or repeated speech, with the noun suffix <na>: {a cih vialna} is what they kept crying out
<vial> after <ci> say, of mocking speech, with the plural <te>: those who say it tauntingly; exact force of <vial> not confirmed
the same word as <vingvial> with its two parts in the other order; the book lists the two as one entry
describes the bright white gleam of snow lying everywhere; meaning inferred from two passages about snow
after <namtui> fragrant: with the sweet smell spreading strongly
of smoke, rising or being blown out in puff after puff, after {za teep}, smoke tobacco, <khusak> and <meikhu>; the other sense is of a smell spreading
of going forward, on and on without stopping or holding back, after a verb of movement such as <mainawt>, advance, and <kantan>, cross over
application for messages and calls on a phone, much used among the Zomi
state in the south-east of Australia; also the name of the British queen after whom many places are named
the capital city of Austria
a country in Southeast Asia; {Vietnam gammi} is a Vietnamese national
of Vietnam, a person from Vietnam; placed before a noun as in {Vietnamese numei}, a Vietnamese woman
one viewing of a video or post on the internet, as counted by the site
the number of times a video on the internet has been watched; the English plural is used unchanged after the number
swing a sword or the arm in order to strike; {viik suk} is swing down
move the arm or a staff with a sweep; {vik to} is swing up and {vik suk} bring down
<vik> swing with the suffix <in>; {a khut vikin} is swinging his arm
keep watch over a place or a person, look out for an enemy, or watch closely for a chance
<vil> watch, with the linking ending <in>
noun of <vil>, watch over: keeping watch; with <mun>, the place of watching
<vil>, watch, with <pa>, a man who does it; {gal vilpa} is the man who keeps watch for the enemy
keep watching someone's steps so as to catch him
<vil> watch with the plural <te>; {gal vilte} is those who keep watch for enemies
after {a tuam}, separate: {a tuam vilvel-in} is quite apart from the ordinary, as a special vow
in {a tuam vilvelin}, quite separately, in a special way
expressive word used in the pair {ving veng} after a verb of going: straight off, without delay
after {ciah pah}, go home at once: describes hurrying off
<vingveng> with <in>, placed after a verb of going: doing it straight away, without stopping or turning aside

terms: try to speed away/attempt to rush off
definition: <vingveng>, straight away, and <sawm>, intend, written as one word after a verb of fleeing such as <taikhiat> or <taisuak>: try to get away at full speed
<vingveng>, hurriedly, and <ziau>, at once, written as one word after a verb of running off or carrying away: off in a flash
expressive word built on <vial>, round: going round in a circle; the book lists it as one entry with <vialving>
placed after a verb such as <it>, love, or <deih>, want: do it firmly and with the whole heart, without wavering
the stringed musical instrument played with a bow; {violin tum} is play the violin
an important guest or person of high rank who is given special treatment
spread quickly and widely on social media; {Viral gawp} is go viral, and {Viral Video} is a video that has spread in this way
state in the east of the United States
a germ too small to see that causes disease and passes from one living thing to another
a visa: the official permission to enter or stay in a country
a clear picture of what a person, a church or an organisation wants to become or to reach, often named together with mission
intensifier with <sa> or <lum>: very hot or warm; also said of a matter or of music that is lively
descriptive word placed after a verb, said of horns that grow out in points, as in {sakhi kii apo viuhveuh}
placed after a word to say that everything is of that kind
<vive> and <bek> written as one word after a noun: nothing but that
word that closes a request or command addressed to several people; {kei vo} is do not
Voice of America, the international radio and news service of the United States, which also broadcasts in Burmese
father of Nahbi, the spy sent from the tribe of Naphtali
a pig; {vok hon} is a herd of pigs
<vok> pig with <cing>, tend, look after
<vok>, pig, with <cing>, tend, and plural <te>: those tending the pigs
<vok> and <khat> written as one word: one pig, mostly a pig given or killed for a feast
a female pig that has not yet had young
a Zomi village of the Tedim area; {Voklaak khuami} is a person of Voklaak
a village of the <Sihzang> area in Chin State, also written {VokLak}
<vok>, pig, and <lu>, head, written as one word: the head of a pig
<vok>, pig, with <no>, young: a young pig
<vok>, pig, with <pi>, big or female: a full-grown pig
a female pig, a sow
<vok>, pig, with <sa>, meat: the flesh of pigs
plural of <vok>, pig
<vok>, pig, with <thau>, fat: the fat of a pig, used as food and in cooking
the game of volleyball, in Zolai also {bawhlung bet}
a person who does a work freely, without pay; {volunteer sem} is serve as a volunteer
people who offer to do a work without pay; the English plural form is used, often with <te>
black or dark in colour, said of horses, hair, skin and the sky
a bear, named beside the lion as a dangerous wild animal
keep or carry something inside, as money in a belt, or a word, a teaching or a rebellious mind in the heart
<vom>, black, capitalised in {Mi Vom pa}, the Black man, for the byname Niger
carry or bring something along with one, as a gift when visiting; probably a spelling of <vom>, carry or hold
<vom>, black, with the linking ending <in>, which joins it to the following verb: turning black and then
<vom> bear with <khe> foot
<vom> bear with <pi>, large or mother animal; in the verses often a she-bear robbed of her cubs
<vom> black with the causative <sak>
<vom> bear with the plural suffix {-te}
the black ones, the colour word <vom> black with plural {-te}, placed after the noun it describes
word of songs and poetry for a child; {sawn leh von} is children and descendants; also in names of family associations
poetic word for a child who is loved, seen in songs and in the title {Vondeih Kep Ding}, on bringing up children
a Zomi village of the Tedim area in Chin State, one of the villages of the Saizang dialect; in lists it follows a person's name as the home village
word of songs and poetry for a dearly held child, from <von>, child, and <tawi>, carry; used after a village or clan name for its sons and daughters, as in the names of village associations
the cherished children of a people or village, said of its members, as in {Zosuan vontawite}, the children of the Zo people
<von> with the plural ending <te>: children, a word of songs and elevated speech
cold or cool; {a vot} is the cold, the opposite of {a sa}, the heat
a leech, the worm that sucks blood; a noun, not {vot}, cold
a vote in an election or a decision; <vote pia> is give a vote, vote for, and {vote ngah} is get votes
<vote>, vote, with <pia>, give: vote in an election; the one voted for stands before it without a marker
<vot>, cold, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not cold, the part that is not cold
<vot>, cold, and <lua>, too much, written as one word: very cold or too cold, of the weather or of things
<vot>, cold, and <mahmah>, very, written as one word
<vot>, cold, with the noun suffix <na>: cold or coolness; {inndei a votna} is the cool room
<vot>, cold, with the causative <sak>: make something cool, as water cools the tongue or shade lessens heat
<votsak>, make cool, and the noun ending <na> written as one word: cooling, or a device that cools; {tuisiang votsakna} is a water cooler
colloquial word that closes a request or command to several people, used like <un>; {pai vou} is go, all of you, and {hong ngai siam vou maw} is please forgive us
a receipt for a payment or a purchase, or a slip that can be exchanged for something
ashes left after burning; {bawngla vu} is the ashes of the heifer; the usual spelling is <vut>
beat or strike a person, as a punishment or in violence; <vuak> is the form used before some endings

not the verb beat: the plural marker <uh> run together with a following <a> or <ah>, written after a verb or after an ending such as <ve>, <kei>, <khit> or <nih>; {hong en ve vua} is look at me, all of you, and {azawh kei vua leh} is if they do not finish
<vua>, beat, and <gawp>, severely, written as one word: beat a person badly

the plural marker <uh> and the place marker <ah> written as one word with the glide that is heard between them, also written <uah>: after a noun that has <a>, <na> or <ka> before it, in or at what belongs to several people, as {a inn vuah}, at their house
town in Suphah near the Arnon, named in a line quoted from the Book of the Wars of the Lord
of a tree or plant, dry up and droop
